title: Drone strike sparks fire at Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl, killing one
detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl overnight — one of Russia's largest, with capacity of roughly 15 million tonnes of crude a year, producing gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other petroleum products. Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Yevrayev said one civilian was killed and 27 people were injured after falling drone debris struck an intercity bus; he said 67 drones were downed over the region, with debris also hitting residential and commercial buildings. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 512 Ukrainian drones were intercepted nationwide over 24 hours. President Zelensky confirmed the strike, part of a wave that also hit a Tu-95MS bomber at Engels air base. It was at least the eighth confirmed strike on Slavneft-YANOS in 2026.

title: Rosneft's Kuibyshev refinery in Samara halted again after drone strike on both crude units
detail: Oil processing at Rosneft's Kuibyshev refinery in Samara city — a distinct facility from the Novokuibyshevsk refinery struck Aug 22 — has been halted since Aug 28 after a Ukrainian drone attack damaged both of the plant's primary crude distillation units, CDU-4 and CDU-5, each with a capacity of about 70,000 barrels per day, two industry sources told Reuters. The refinery, which accounts for roughly 1.3% of Russia's total refining throughput and produces gasoline, diesel and fuel oil, had only just resumed operations on Aug 21 after completing a major overhaul that began July 1 — meaning it was shut down again about a week after restarting.

media.caption: Kuibyshev refinery in Samara, halted again after an Aug 28 2026 drone strike damaged both crude distillation units
